title: Deferred scan optimizer and tenant slice cache for low-tail dashboard queries
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Some dashboard queries that scan high-cardinality time ranges exhibit long-tail read latencies (95p/99p) caused by large on-demand segment scans and tenant fanout. Existing prefix/KV caching mitigates hot prefixes but does not handle large, sparse queries that cross many microshards.

Proposal: Implement a deferred-scan optimizer combined with a tenant-slice in-memory cache (tenant-slice-cache) that schedules and coalesces background materialization of frequently accessed scan windows. The optimizer will: (1) use telemetry to detect recurring heavy scan patterns, (2) choose a coalescing window and slice size per tenant, (3) schedule low-priority background reads to pre-populate slices into the cache, and (4) serve fast path reads from the slice cache while letting rare ad-hoc queries fall back to on-demand scans.

Key ideas: adaptive slice sizing, telemetry-driven candidate detection, background materialization with rate limits, eviction pinned by per-tenant memory budgets, and API-level hints for canarying the fast-path. The feature should be rolloutable per-tenant and include observability (hit/miss rates, materialization latency, extra IO, memory usage).
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile dashboard query latency for targeted heavy queries reduced by >=40% compared to baseline
Slice cache hit rate >= 70% for experiment tenants within 2 weeks of materialization
Background materialization does not increase overall query error rate or violate SLOs for other tenants
Configurable per-tenant budget and TTL are available via admin Console and CLI
Autoscaling/backpressure paths in place: if materialization queue grows > threshold, background work is throttled and no additional tenant slices are scheduled
notes: Initial telemetry analysis (2025-01-06) identified 18 tenant query patterns responsible for 42% of long-tail read amplification over the prior 30d window

Prototype implemented with a separate materializer worker pool and a memory-backed LRU for tenant slices; proof-of-concept shows 95p latency drop from ~420ms to ~180ms for a sampled heavy dashboard query (single-tenant test)
Measured trade-offs: materialization increased steady-state memory by ~18% for the experiment cluster and introduced ~12% extra read IO during warm-up windows; baseline caching unchanged
Eviction: adopt a two-tier policy: per-tenant soft budget with global reclaim; prioritize slices by recency*access_count score
Compatibility: interacts with existing KV cache — decide on unified lookup order (slice-cache -> KV prefix -> storage scan) to avoid duplicate work
Fallback behavior: if slice materialization is incomplete, query planner will fetch missing ranges and insert into transient per-request aggregator to keep correctness

2025-01-12: Completed telemetry query set and candidate pattern classifier. Added test harness for simulated tenant query traces. Baseline metrics captured. (Marcus)
2025-01-15: PoC materializer worker created. First end-to-end run on staging shows 45% 95p reduction for target queries. Observability hooks added to trace materialization steps. (Marcus, Diego)
2025-01-18: PM review: emphasize admin controls and cost transparency. PM requested per-tenant projected IO/cost estimate in Console before enabling. (Sofia)

2025-01-20: Security review pre-check: no sensitive data stored in slice cache; slices are transient and encrypted at rest when persisted to swap. Security okayed continuing with implementation but full review on production rollout. (Security)
2025-01-23: Prototype profiling: materializer increases memory pressure on nodes with co-located query workers. Decided to isolate worker pool on dedicated nodes to bound impact. (Marcus)

2025-01-25: Integration tests added for unified lookup order and correctness under partial slice availability. Next: implement admin surface and cost estimator, then plan 2-week canary on 3 low-risk tenants.
